expansion_contract.fact_row: verified official-source, canonical-state, workflow-evidence or acceptance-contract fact
expansion_contract.boundary_row: prevents summary counts, residential products, output-area classifications, speed taxonomies, active-line performance or FWA composites from being promoted to exact January 2026 all-premises postcode or parcel coverage without accepted r2 bytes and hardened postjoin evidence

source_routes.name: Spring 2026 fixed coverage and full-fibre take-up v2 data note
Spring 2026 fixed product and field-matrix screenshots

facts.detail: The terminal heartbeat has no active owner lease.
No active or over-15-minute PENDING execution exists.

guard_streams.write_limit: No second task, owner takeover or parallel runner is permitted.

facts.detail: The exact 11,013-row output JSONL remains empty.
Corrected r2 bytes, members, hashes, schema and row-count acceptance remain unverified.

guard_streams.write_limit: No candidate or 3/4 promotion before exact r2 and hardened postjoin acceptance.

facts.detail: An active full-fibre line is a connection providing an active broadband service to a residential or business customer as of January 2026.
UK-and-nations full-fibre take-up is supplied through the accompanying summary tables rather than the local-authority CSV.

guard_streams.write_limit: Active-line take-up is not maximum available postcode speed.

facts.detail: The UK-and-nations product contains separate percentage-of-premises and number-of-premises measures.
The documented snapshot-date field is Jan-26.

guard_streams.write_limit: Summary percentages and counts cannot replace exact postcode records.

facts.detail: The all-premises census-output-area product documents 238,878 rows and a 26 MB file.
The residential census-output-area product documents 238,850 rows and a 26 MB file.

guard_streams.write_limit: All-premises and residential output-area products must not be interchanged.

guard_streams.source: Spring 2026 fixed data note and screenshot

facts.detail: The corrected all-premises postcode product comprises 121 internal r2 files with 1,741,096 documented rows and 165 MB uncompressed size.
The separate residential postcode product comprises 121 r1 files with 1,606,191 documented rows and 151 MB uncompressed size.

guard_streams.write_limit: The residential r1 product cannot satisfy the all-premises r2 task contract.

facts.detail: Output-area products use the 2021 census framework for England, Northern Ireland and Wales.
Scottish output areas use the 2022 census framework.

guard_streams.write_limit: Cross-nation output-area identifiers require their documented census vintage.

facts.detail: The summary speed taxonomy distinguishes Premise Base, Unclassified and less-than-2-Mbit/s categories.
A distinct category identifies premises below 10 Mbit/s download or below 1 Mbit/s upload.

guard_streams.write_limit: Unclassified and below-threshold premises are not the same population.

facts.detail: The summary taxonomy separately reports at least 10, 24, 30, 100 and 300 Mbit/s categories.
Full-fibre and gigabit-capable categories are separately represented from numerical speed thresholds.

guard_streams.write_limit: Technology labels and speed-threshold labels must not be collapsed.

facts.detail: Maximum-download distributions use the documented intervals 0-2, 2-5, 5-10, 10-30 and 30-300 Mbit/s.
Premises with maximum download speed of at least 300 Mbit/s form a separate upper category.

guard_streams.write_limit: Band percentages do not provide a measured speed for an individual parcel.

facts.detail: Next Generation Access is defined as networks consisting wholly or partly of optical fibre and capable of delivering broadband.
Ofcom's NGA analysis includes full fibre, HFC, VDSL and G.Fast while excluding ADSL.

guard_streams.write_limit: NGA classification is not equivalent to full fibre or gigabit capability.

facts.detail: The fixed-or-FWA decent-broadband deficit includes fixed broadband, WISP and Mobile FWA and also includes unmatched records and zero predicted speeds.
The separate decent-broadband-from-FWA field is documented as access from a WISP at the 10-down and 1-up threshold.

guard_streams.write_limit: Composite deficit and WISP-availability fields have different populations and cannot be substituted.

facts.detail: The fixed-broadband coverage download provides maximum available speed information and accompanies each Connected Nations publication.
The fixed-broadband performance product covers speeds reported for active customer connections and full-fibre take-up by local authority.

guard_streams.write_limit: Availability and active-connection performance are distinct products.

facts.detail: Ofcom no longer publishes a fixed-performance postcode file following the July 2024 data-collection methodology change.
Ofcom considers overall average download-speed analysis robust down to local-authority level but not postcode level.

guard_streams.write_limit: Local-authority performance averages must not be downscaled to postcodes or parcels.

guard_streams.source: Connected Nations FAQs and canonical workflow evidence

facts.detail: Connected Nations is currently published twice yearly, normally with a main year-end report and a spring interim update.
The available current-HEAD search returned zero PR-triggered workflow runs and no candidate, measured-speed or accuracy promotion was made.

guard_streams.write_limit: Publication cadence and absent host evidence cannot satisfy exact r2 acceptance.
